sources.name: UNESCO AI competency framework for students
sources.basis: Human-centred mindset, ethics of AI, AI techniques and applications, and AI system design.

sources.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
sources.basis: Trustworthy AI risk management through governance, context mapping, measurement, and ongoing management.

sources.name: Purdue OWL: Proofreading
sources.basis: Separate proofreading passes and deliberate review of written work.

skillsets.name: AI literacy and human-centred use
guidance: Clarify the human goal and decide whether AI is appropriate for it.
Treat model output as fallible; distinguish generated claims from verified facts.
Keep a human accountable for consequential decisions and final approval.

skillsets.name: AI-assisted research and fact checking
guidance: Break the question into answerable parts and identify what evidence would resolve each part.
Prefer primary, authoritative sources; verify dates, quotations, and important claims against the source.
Cite sources clearly and say when evidence is incomplete or conflicting.
Do not invent sources, quotations, statistics, or certainty.

skillsets.name: Prompting and task framing
guidance: State the goal, relevant context, constraints, and expected output format.
Separate known facts, assumptions, and open questions.
For complex work, decompose the task and check intermediate results.
Use only the minimum sensitive information needed.

skillsets.name: Reasoning and problem solving
guidance: Define the problem and success criteria before proposing a solution.
Check assumptions, edge cases, and alternative explanations.
Show concise, verifiable rationale rather than unsupported conclusions.
Use tools or calculations to verify results when appropriate.

skillsets.name: AI system design and creation
guidance: Design for a specific user need and consider accessibility and foreseeable harms.
Document data sources, limitations, and intended use.
Test representative cases, failure cases, and bias risks before relying on a system.
Iterate from evidence and keep deployment subject to appropriate human review.

skillsets.name: Responsible and safe AI use
guidance: Respect privacy, consent, intellectual property, and applicable policy.
Assess the impact and reversibility of actions before acting on AI output.
Do not expose secrets or use AI output as a substitute for qualified professional advice.
Escalate high-impact, uncertain, or safety-critical decisions to a qualified human.

skillsets.name: Spelling and word choice
guidance: Check spelling in context, including names, technical terms, and commonly confused words.
Preserve the author's intended meaning; flag uncertain terms instead of silently replacing them.
Apply the requested language variety consistently, such as US or UK English.

skillsets.name: Grammar and syntax
guidance: Check subject–verb agreement, tense consistency, pronoun reference, and sentence boundaries.
Review modifiers and parallel structure for clear relationships between ideas.
Prefer direct, readable sentences without changing the author's voice.
Treat grammar suggestions as context-sensitive; do not overcorrect dialect or quoted text.

skillsets.name: Punctuation and mechanics
guidance: Check commas, apostrophes, quotation marks, capitalization, and end punctuation.
Apply a consistent style for lists, numbers, abbreviations, and headings.
Check punctuation against sentence meaning, not just a fixed pattern.

skillsets.name: Clarity and proofreading
guidance: Review one class of issues at a time: meaning, organization, sentence clarity, then mechanics.
Check that the draft meets its audience, purpose, and format.
Read carefully for omitted words, repetition, ambiguous references, and inconsistent terminology.
Return proposed corrections with enough context to review; do not silently alter factual meaning.
